mainTopic: A lost and found גט: when it may be returned, the different answers to the contradiction, סימנין, and how long a delay counts as 'not immediately'.
overview: Our משנה says a lost גט that was found is valid only if it was found right away. Other sources, a משנה in בבא מציעא and a ברייתא, seem to return a found גט even after a long time. רבה said our משנה deals with a town known to have two men with the same names. רבי זירא said it depends on whether caravans pass through often, and the גמרא explains why each one built his question on a different source. רבי ירמיה says the גט is returned when the witnesses signed only one גט with these names. רב אשי says it is returned when the owner gives a very exact mark, because he is unsure whether ordinary סימנין work by Torah law. A story about רבה בר בר חנה, who lost a גט in the study hall, shows the same doubt about סימנין. Finally, a ברייתא lists opinions on how long a delay counts as 'not immediately,' and says a clear mark still works after a delay. The amud ends by starting the next case in the משנה, a גט found tied in a pouch, purse or ring, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing רבי זירא's contradiction from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a found גט is returned to the woman whenever the husband admits writing it, which seems to mean even after a long time. That clashes with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the husband admits that he wrote it, in any event he should return it to the woman, and that seems to apply even after a long time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote from the ברייתא that רבי זירא uses to challenge our משנה. Since no time limit is mentioned, he reads it as 'even after a long time.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a lost גט that was not found right away is פסול. The ברייתא gives only one condition, that the husband admits writing it, and says nothing about time. So it seems to allow returning the גט even after a long delay, which contradicts our משנה.

phrases.english: When the husband admits, in any event —
he should return it to the woman,
and even after a long time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי זירא's contradiction, which started before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that a lost גט not found right away is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives no time limit, so it seems to allow returning the גט even after a long time.

steps.title: רבי זירא's answer: it depends on caravans
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה deals with a place where caravans pass through often. The ברייתא deals with a place where they don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answers: Here (our משנה), it is a place where caravans are common. There (the ברייתא), it is a place where caravans are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the contradiction by placing each source in a different kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where many travelers pass, another man with the same names may have dropped the גט, so after a long time it cannot be trusted. Where few travelers pass, that worry is unlikely, so the גט can be returned even later.

keyTerms.meaning: here... there (splitting two sources into two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא: a found גט is not trusted after a long time where caravans are common, but is trusted where they are not.

phrases.english: And he answers:
Here, in a place where caravans are common,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is our משנה, where the גט is not returned. Lots of travelers means it might belong to someone else.

phrases.english: there, in a place where caravans are not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different kind of place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and our משנה seem to argue about whether a גט found after a long time may be returned.
steps.terutzMaskana: They don't argue. Our משנה is a place with frequent caravans, and the ברייתא is a place without them.

steps.title: First version: רבי זירא agrees with רבה
steps.stepSummary: One version says רבי זירא's caravan rule applies only when it is known that two people with the same names live there, which matches רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: Even where caravans are common, it is not returned only when it was established that there are two people with the same names. This is the same as רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins comparing רבי זירא with רבה. This first version says the two agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Caravans alone are not enough. The גט is held back only if we also know there are two people with the same names. That is exactly רבה's condition, so the two אמוראים reach the same ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: it was established (that two people share the same names)
and this is the same as

phrases.english: There are those who say:
And that is when it was established
phrases.notes: He means it was established that two men in town share the husband's name and the wife's name, as in רבה's case.

phrases.english: that it should not be returned,
and this is the same as Rabba;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי זירא's answer from Step 2 and compares it with רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a caravan place, the גט is held back only if it is known there are two people with the same names. This matches רבה.

steps.title: Second version: רבי זירא argues with רבה
steps.stepSummary: Another version says that where caravans are common, the גט is not returned even without proof of two people with the same names, so רבי זירא disagrees with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: Even though it was not established that there are two people with the same names, it should not be returned, and he disagrees with רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite version: frequent caravans alone are enough to hold back the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, many travelers already create enough doubt, with no proof of a second couple with the same names needed. רבה requires that proof, so here the two אמוראים truly disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: Two versions: either רבי זירא needs proof of two people with the same names, which matches רבה, or caravans alone are enough, which disagrees with רבה.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
even though it was not established,
it should not be returned,
and he disagrees with Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הוּחְזְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a caravan place, the גט is not returned even without proof of two people with the same names. This disagrees with רבה.

steps.title: Why did each אמורא choose a different source?
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense that רבה used the משנה, since a משנה is a stronger source for a challenge. But why didn't רבי זירא also use the משנה like רבה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבה did not ask like רבי זירא, because for him a challenge from a משנה is stronger. But רבי זירא, what is the reason he did not ask like רבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא challenged from a ברייתא and not from the משנה in בבא מציעא that רבה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא, so רבה's choice is easy to understand. The puzzle is רבי זירא: why give up the stronger source? This sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Granted that Rabba
did not say like Rabbi Zeira,
phrases.notes: He means רבה didn't challenge from the ברייתא the way רבי זירא did.

phrases.english: for him, the mishna is stronger to raise a difficulty from;
but Rabbi Zeira,
what is the reason he did not say like Rabba?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבָּה לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from comparing the rulings to comparing the sources each Amora used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי זירא did not challenge from the stronger source, the משנה in בבא מציעא, as רבה did.

steps.title: רבי זירא did not read the משנה as 'even after a long time'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא would say that the משנה in בבא מציעא never says 'even after a long time.' It may mean only a גט found right away, as our משנה rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: Does it teach, 'If he said give, they give, even after a long time'? Perhaps it means 'If he said give, they give,' only as we hold, when it is found right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי זירא saw no real contradiction in the משנה in בבא מציעא, so he had to use the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's challenge depended on reading 'even after a long time' into the משנה. רבי זירא says the משנה can be read as talking only about a גט found right away, so it fits our משנה perfectly. Only the ברייתא, with its broad wording, gave him a real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: does it teach? (meaning: it doesn't say that)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא used the ברייתא because the משנה in בבא מציעא can be read as dealing only with a גט found right away, so it does not contradict our משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מִי קָתָנֵי' is not a real question. It means 'the text doesn't actually say that.' The 'even after a long time' was only רבה's inference.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
Does it teach:
If he said 'Give,' they give,
and even after a long time?
Perhaps: if he said 'Give,' they give
as we hold — immediately.
phrases.notes: 'As we hold' points back to our משנה, which says a lost גט found right away is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה in בבא מציעא does not clearly mean 'even after a long time.' It can be read as a גט found right away, so it raises no contradiction. Only the ברייתא did.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: The witnesses signed only one such גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the lost גט is returned only when the witnesses say they never signed any other גט for a man with this name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The case is where the witnesses say, 'We never signed any גט of יוסף בן שמעון except this one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the contradiction about returning a lost גט. רבי ירמיה says it is returned only when the witnesses confirm that this is the only גט they ever signed with these names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה worries that a found גט might belong to a different couple with the same names. If the witnesses say they signed only one גט with these names, that worry goes away. So the משנה in בבא מציעא and the ברייתא are talking about this special case.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses, here the ones who signed the גט

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is a case where the witnesses say:
We never signed
except on one גט
of Yosef ben Shimon.
phrases.notes: יוסף בן שמעון is just a sample name, like saying 'John Smith.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר, כְּגוֹן דְּקָאָמְרִי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the contradiction instead of the caravan answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in בבא מציעא and the ברייתא seem to return any found גט, which clashes with our משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: They return the גט only when the witnesses confirm they signed no other גט with these names

steps.title: If so, why does this even need to be said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the witnesses confirm it, obviously the גט is hers, so why would a source need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's answer. If the case is that clear, why would the משנה need to tell us to return the גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source should teach something we would not know by ourselves. If the witnesses already confirm whose גט it is, returning it looks obvious. So it seems there is nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (it seems obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי ירמיה's answer for making the ruling seem obvious
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the witnesses clearly identify the גט, returning it is obvious and needs no teaching

steps.title: It teaches that we do not worry about matching names and matching witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed because we might have worried about another גט with the same names and witnesses who happen to have the same names.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we should worry that it just happened that the names matched and the witnesses' names matched. So it teaches us that we do not worry about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ruling still teaches something: we do not worry about a very unlikely coincidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might worry about a second גט with the same couple's names, signed by different witnesses who happen to have the same names as these witnesses. The ruling teaches that this double coincidence is too far-fetched to worry about. So the witnesses' statement is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A name like the same name

phrases.english: You might have said we should worry
that perhaps it happened that a name matched a name
and witnesses matched witnesses
phrases.notes: He means different witnesses who happen to have the same names as these witnesses.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would worry about a double coincidence of names and witnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a coincidence is not a concern, so the גט is returned

steps.title: רב אשי: The owner gives a very clear identifying mark
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the גט is returned when the owner says there is a hole next to a specific letter, which counts as a סימן מובהק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where the owner says, 'There is a hole in it next to a certain letter,' because that is a very clear identifying mark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to the contradiction. רב אשי says the lost גט is returned when the owner gives a very exact mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole next to a specific letter is so exact that it could not fit another גט by chance. So the worry about another couple with the same names goes away. The משנה in בבא מציעא and the ברייתא are talking about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A very clear, exact identifying mark

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is a case where he says:

phrases.aramaic: נֶקֶב יֵשׁ בּוֹ בְּצַד אוֹת פְּלוֹנִית,
phrases.english: There is a hole in it next to a certain letter,
since that is a very clear identifying mark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer to the same contradiction, besides the caravan answer and רבי ירמיה's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seem to return a found גט with no special proof
steps.terutzMaskana: They return it only when there is a סימן מובהק

steps.title: Only an exact hole counts, not just any hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes clear that רב אשי needs the hole's exact place, next to a certain letter. Just saying 'there is a hole' is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only when he says next to a certain letter, because that is a very clear mark. But if he just says 'there is a hole,' no, we do not return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out exactly what רב אשי requires. It is preparing for the next step, which explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain hole is an ordinary סימן, a regular identifying mark. It is not exact enough. For a גט, רב אשי accepts only the exact kind of mark.

phrases.english: And only when it is next to a certain letter,
since that is a very clear identifying mark,
but just a hole, no;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the limit of רב אשי's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a סימן מובהק lets us return a lost גט, not an ordinary סימן

steps.title: Why: רב אשי is unsure whether סימנין are from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי is unsure whether returning lost things by ordinary סימנין is a Torah law or a rabbinic law, so for a גט he relies only on a סימן מובהק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is unsure about סימנין: are they from the Torah or from the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב אשי requires an exact mark. He is unsure how strong ordinary marks are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ordinary סימנין work only by rabbinic law, they may not be strong enough to settle a Torah matter like a גט. A סימן מובהק works by Torah law according to everyone. So for a גט, רב אשי relies only on an exact mark.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks used to claim a lost item

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction about returning a lost גט gets several answers. רבה, on the previous amud, said our משנה deals with a town known to have two men with the same names. רבי זירא said it depends on whether caravans are common. רבי ירמיה said the other sources deal with witnesses who signed only one such גט. רב אשי said they deal with a סימן מובהק. רב אשי needs an exact mark because he is unsure whether ordinary סימנין are from the Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying סימנין are rabbinic. He is unsure, so he plays it safe with a גט and uses only the kind of mark everyone agrees works by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of סימנין דאורייתא או דרבנן comes up in many places in ש״ס, especially in בבא מציעא, and it affects how much we can rely on identifying marks.

phrases.english: He is unsure about identifying marks:
whether they are from the Torah or from the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ סִימָנִין אִי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אִי דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the limit in step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because of the doubt about ordinary סימנין, a lost גט is returned only with a סימן מובהק

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה loses a גט in the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה lost a גט in the בית מדרש. He said he could identify it either by a סימן or by recognizing it on sight, and they returned it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה lost a גט in the study hall. He said: 'If you need a sign, I have a sign on it. If you need recognition by sight, I can recognize it.' They gave it back to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case of a lost גט being returned to the person who lost it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה offered two different ways to prove the גט was his: a סימן, a sign he could describe, or טביעות עין, recognizing it by sight. The story tells us they gave the גט back, but not which of the two reasons they relied on. That open question is what the next step picks up.

keyTerms.meaning: recognizing something by sight, without describing a specific mark

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana
lost a bill of divorce in the study hall.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: אִי סִימָנָא – אִית לִי בְּגַוֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: He said: If a sign is needed, I have one for it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי טְבִיעוּת – עֵינָא אִית לִי בְּגַוֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: If recognition by sight is needed, I have that for it too.
They returned it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִירְכַס לֵיהּ גִּיטָּא בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי's doubt about whether סימנין count from the Torah, the גמרא brings a story where that same question comes up in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost גט was returned to רבה בר בר חנה after he said he could identify it by a sign or by sight.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה is unsure why they trusted him
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה did not know whether the גט was returned because of his סימן, which would mean they hold סימנין are from the Torah, or because of his טביעות עין, which is trusted only from a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I don't know whether they returned it because of the sign, which means they hold that signs count by Torah law, or because of recognition by sight, which is trusted only from a Torah scholar and not from an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה looks back on what happened and admits he cannot tell which reason the רבנן used to give him the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they relied on his סימן, that shows they hold סימנין דאורייתא, so signs would work for anyone. If they relied on his טביעות עין, that is a special trust given only to a צורבא מדרבנן. In that case an ordinary person could not get a גט back this way. The story ends without settling the question.

keyTerms.meaning: the view that identifying signs count by Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The story leaves two possibilities open: either סימנין are דאורייתא and work for anyone, or a תלמיד חכם is trusted when he says he recognizes something by sight.

phrases.english: He said: I do not know
whether they returned it because of the sign,
and they hold that signs count by Torah law,
or because of recognition by sight,
and that is only for a Torah scholar,
but not for an ordinary person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: לָא יָדַעְנָא אִי מִשּׁוּם סִימָנָא אַהְדְּרוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the story in step 13 and asks which of the two reasons the רבנן actually used.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story cannot prove that סימנין are דאורייתא, because the רבנן may have relied on a תלמיד חכם's recognition by sight instead.

steps.title: What counts as 'not immediately'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and if not, it is invalid' and brings a ברייתא that asks how long a delay counts as 'not immediately.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And if not, it is invalid.' The רבנן taught: What counts as 'not immediately'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and sets up a question. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a found גט is valid if it was found right away, but invalid if not. The ברייתא now asks how much time has to pass before it no longer counts as 'right away.' The worry is that during a delay, a different גט could have been dropped there.

phrases.english: And if not, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words: if the גט was not found right away, it is invalid.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What is considered 'not immediately'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of סימנין for now and goes back to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long a delay makes a found גט count as 'not found immediately,' so that it is invalid.

steps.title: רבי נתן: long enough for a caravan to pass and camp
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says 'not immediately' means a delay long enough for a caravan to pass by and set up camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: It means a delay long enough for a caravan to pass by and camp there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the first answer to the question of how long a delay counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן measures the delay by how long it takes a caravan to pass by and camp. That is enough time for many people to pass through, so another גט could have been dropped there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
When there was a delay as long as it takes
for a caravan to pass by and camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: שֶׁשָּׁהָה כְּדֵי שֶׁתַּעֲבוֹר שְׁיָירָא וְתִשְׁרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Not immediately' means a delay long enough for a caravan to pass by and camp.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: it depends on whether anyone passed by
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it still counts as immediate as long as someone was watching and saw that nobody passed there. A second version of his view says the test is that nobody stopped there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: It counts as immediate as long as a person stood and saw that nobody passed there. Some say: as long as nobody stopped there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second answer. This one does not use a fixed amount of time; it looks at what actually happened in that spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the length of the delay does not matter. What matters is whether anyone could have dropped another גט there. The יש אומרים version is easier: people passing by is fine, as long as nobody stopped in that place.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
As long as there is a person standing and watching
that no one passed there.
And some say:
phrases.notes: This gives another version of what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said.

phrases.english: As long as no one stopped there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רבי נתן's to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The test is whether anyone passed by, or in the other version, whether anyone stopped there. It is not a fixed amount of time.

steps.title: Measuring by the time to write or read a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי says 'immediately' means less than the time it takes to write a גט. רבי יצחק says less than the time to read it. אחרים say less than the time to write it and read it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: As long as it takes to write the גט. רבי יצחק says: As long as it takes to read it. אחרים say: As long as it takes to write it and read it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives three more answers. Each one measures the delay by the time it takes to deal with a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three opinions use the גט itself as the measure. If enough time passed for someone to write a גט, read one, or do both, then a different גט could have ended up there.
steps.whatToRemember: There are five measures of 'not immediately': a caravan passing and camping (רבי נתן); whether anyone passed or stopped there (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר); the time to write a גט (רבי); the time to read one (רבי יצחק); the time to write and read one (אחרים).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב אֶת הַגֵּט.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: As long as it takes to write the bill of divorce.
Rabbi Yitzchak says: As long as it takes to read it.
Others say: As long as it takes to write it and read it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב אֶת הַגֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more opinions to the same list of answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The delay is measured by the time it takes to write a גט, to read it, or to do both.

steps.title: Even after a delay, a clear sign works
steps.stepSummary: Even if there was a delay, a גט with clear סימנין, such as a hole next to a certain letter, can be identified by those signs and is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if there was a delay, if the גט has signs, they can testify about it, for example when they say: 'There is a hole in it next to such-and-such a letter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching adds an exception to the delay rule: a clear identifying sign can still save the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a delay makes the found גט invalid, because it might be a different גט. A very specific סימן, like a hole next to a certain letter, takes away that worry, because another גט would not have that same mark. This is the same kind of sign רב אשי required in steps 10 and 11.

keyTerms.meaning: they testify about it, identifying it

phrases.english: And even if there was a delay,
if it has signs, they testify about it,
for example, when they say: There is a hole in it
next to such-and-such a letter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁהָה, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ סִימָנִין – מְעִידִים עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the delay rules from steps 15–18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after a delay, a גט can be identified by a clear sign such as a hole next to a certain letter.

steps.title: General size is not a valid sign
steps.stepSummary: Testimony about the גט's general physical features, like whether it is long or short, does not count as a sign for identifying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they do not testify about signs of its body, such as saying 'it is long' or 'it is short.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching sets a limit: not every description counts as a sign that can identify the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being long or short is too common a feature. Many documents could look the same in that way, so it does not prove this is the same גט. Only a specific mark, like the one in step 19, is good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: general features of the document itself, like its size

steps.whatToRemember: A specific mark, like a hole next to a certain letter, can identify a found גט even after a delay. General features like size cannot.

phrases.english: But they do not testify about signs of its body,
phrases.notes: 'Its body' here means the גט itself, its general shape and size.

phrases.english: such as when they say: long or short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of step 19 by saying which kinds of signs do not count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: General physical features of a גט, like its length, cannot be used to identify it.

steps.title: Next line of the משנה: a גט found tied in a pouch, purse or ring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה: a גט found tied in a pouch, a purse, or a ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found it tied up in a pouch, in a purse, or in a ring,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה to set up the next discussion. The ruling and the analysis continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is different from a גט just lying on the ground. A גט tied inside a container may be easier to recognize. The rule for this case has not been stated yet.

phrases.english: If he found it tied in a pouch,
in a purse, or in a ring,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which gives the ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the delay discussion to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of a גט found tied in a pouch, purse or ring. The ruling comes in the next section.
